title: Koalas Have Fingerprints Almost Identical to Yours

scenes.text: Koalas have fingerprints. Almost identical to yours.
Even under a microscope, experts struggle to tell a koala's print from a human's.
A scientist in Adelaide noticed it in the 1990s, and warned police to keep it in mind at crime scenes.
Our last common ancestor lived over 100 million years ago. Even wombats and kangaroos don't have prints.
They evolved them separately, for the same job as ours: gripping thin branches and grabbing leaves.
So if a koala is ever fingerprinted, good luck. Almost identical to yours.

description:
Koalas have fingerprints that are almost identical to human fingerprints.
In the 1990s, forensic anthropologist Maciej Henneberg at the University of Adelaide found that koala prints are so human-like that they can be hard to tell apart even under a microscope. Koalas evolved them independently, probably for gripping eucalyptus branches.
Which other animal do you think has fingerprints?
first_comment: Chimps and gorillas have fingerprints too, but they're our relatives. Koalas invented theirs from scratch. Which other animal would you check next?
